blocks.text: 1. Tool Calling

blocks.alt: A model requests a function, which the application executes

blocks.text: Agentic RAG introduced an agent choosing between tools rather than following one fixed pipeline. Tool Calling, letting the model invoke a specific function with structured arguments, is the concrete mechanism that makes that choice possible, opening this dedicated Agentic RAG module.
The model requests a named function and supplies structured arguments for it.
2. The Model Requests A Function, It Does Not Run It
The model itself never executes any code directly.
It only outputs a request naming a function and the arguments to call it with.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Actor","What it actually does"],"rows":[["Model","Outputs a request naming a function and its arguments"],["Application code","Actually executes the requested function"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Defining Available Tools Upfront

blocks.alt: Tool A and tool B are available tools

blocks.text: As with defining the expected fields in Structured Output, each available tool is described with a name, a purpose, and its expected argument schema.
The model can only request tools it was actually told about.
4. The Model Chooses Whether To Call A Tool

blocks.alt: A query goes through a model that chooses to call a tool or answer directly

blocks.text: Given a query, the model decides whether answering directly is enough or a tool call is needed.
Not every query actually requires invoking a tool at all.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A greeting like hello needs no tool call at all, while a question needing today's data requires the model to request a live lookup tool instead.

blocks.text: 5. The Application Executes The Requested Call

blocks.alt: A requested call goes through the application to produce a result

blocks.text: The surrounding application code receives the tool request and actually executes it.
The model waits for that real execution result before continuing.
6. Feeding The Result Back To The Model

blocks.alt: A tool result goes back to the model to produce the final response

blocks.text: The tool's actual output is passed back into the conversation as new context.
The model then continues, now grounded in that real result rather than a guess.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","What happens"],"rows":[["Model requests a tool","Names a function and supplies arguments"],["Application executes it","Runs the real function and captures the output"],["Result fed back","Model continues grounded in the real output"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Validating Arguments Before Executing

blocks.alt: The model arguments are validated for whether they are valid

blocks.text: As with validating the parsed result in JSON Output, the requested arguments still need validation before the real function actually runs.
A malformed or unsafe argument should be rejected before execution.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A tool call requesting a negative page size or an out of range date, should be caught by validation before the underlying function runs, not discovered only after it fails or misbehaves.

8. Tool Calling Is The Foundation Of Agentic RAG
As with the agent calls tools not just a retriever in Agentic RAG, every other capability in this module is built on top of this basic request and execute mechanism.
Planning, reflection, and memory all rely on tool calling underneath.
9. Recognizing When Tool Calling Is Worth Adding To A RAG Assistant

blocks.alt: Needing actions beyond text generation points toward tool calling

blocks.text: Tasks needing real computation or external data require tool calling.
Questions fully answerable from retrieved context alone need no tool calls at all.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Letting the model execute code directly instead of only requesting a tool call.
Skipping argument validation and passing unchecked input straight into a real function.
Defining tools without a clear name, purpose, or argument schema the model can follow.
Adding tool calling to a RAG assistant that only ever needs answers from retrieved context.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Tool calling lets the model invoke a specific function with structured arguments.
The model only requests a function by name; it never executes code directly.
Each available tool is described upfront with a name, purpose, and argument schema.
The model decides whether a query needs a tool call or can be answered directly.
The surrounding application code actually executes the requested tool call.
The tool's real output is fed back into the conversation, grounding the model's next step.
Requested arguments still need validation before the real function actually runs.
Tool calling is the foundation every other capability in this module builds on.
